title: Tag Management Studio Cutover P0 Freeze
summary: Temporary working inventory of the pre-cutover tag data, routes, APIs, activity actions, frontend, tests, and external consumers.
content_html:
Tag Management Studio Cutover P0 Freeze

Purpose

This is the temporary evidence baseline for TMS-P0. It records the live pre-cutover contract so TMS-P1 through TMS-P3 can prove ownership and route changes without changing tag meaning.

The delivery remains the implementation tracker. Retire this note at delivery closeout after stable conclusions have moved to current owner documentation.

Freeze captured: 2026-07-25 17:57:53 +0100.

All paths are relative to the repository root. Hashes are SHA-256 over the exact file bytes.

Additional count and envelope evidence:

  • registry: tag_registry_v1, updated 2026-06-24T19:19:09Z; 80 subject, 45 domain, 71 form, and 79 theme tags; policy allows subject, domain, form, and theme;
  • aliases: tag_aliases_v1, updated 2026-03-12T19:44:52Z; 83 canonical target references across 82 aliases;
  • assignments: tag_assignments_v1, updated 2026-04-29T10:28:03Z; 5 series tag rows, 3 Work override records, 5 Work tag rows, and 10 total assignment tag rows;
  • groups: tag_groups_v1, updated 2026-03-03T16:29:52Z; the stored order is domain, form, subject, theme.

The config-owned display and coverage order remains subject, domain, form, theme. The different order in tag-groups.json is existing source order, not a discrepancy to normalize during the move.

Routes And Reads

The Analytics shell currently mounts these five live routes:

route id path template entry module main reads
tag_groups /analytics/tag-groups/ tag-groups.html tag-groups.js groups
tag_registry /analytics/tag-registry/ tag-registry.html tag-registry.js registry, aliases, assignments, groups, public series index
tag_aliases /analytics/tag-aliases/ tag-aliases.html tag-aliases.js aliases, registry, groups
series_tags /analytics/series-tags/ series-tags.html series-tags.js assignments, registry, groups, public series index
series_tag_editor /analytics/series-tag-editor/?series=<series-id> series-tag-editor.html series-tag-editor-page.js and dynamically loaded analytics-tag-editor.js assignments, aliases, registry, public series and Work indexes

The server exposes GET /health as a process check. Under /analytics/api it also exposes:

  • GET /health for tag-write capability discovery;
  • GET /tag-registry, /tag-aliases, /tag-assignments, and /tag-groups for the four canonical payloads.

The browser reads public catalogue context from /assets/data/series_index.json and /assets/data/works_index.json. The Series Tag Editor also receives media and public-site settings through runtime config.

Writes, Plans, And Transactions

All listed paths are mounted below /analytics/api. OPTIONS mirrors every POST path.

endpoint contract
POST /save-tags save or remove one Series or Work assignment row from series_id, optional work_id, keep_work, and normalized weighted tags
POST /import-tag-assignments-preview validate an offline-session assignment payload and report applicable, conflict, invalid, and missing Series rows without writing
POST /import-tag-assignments apply the previously represented assignment import using explicit per-Series conflict resolutions
POST /import-tag-registry add or merge sanitized canonical tag rows; also supplies the one-tag create path
POST /import-tag-aliases add or merge sanitized alias rows; also supplies the one-alias create path
POST /delete-tag-alias delete one confirmed alias
POST /mutate-tag-alias-preview, POST /mutate-tag-alias preview then apply alias key, description, or target edits
POST /promote-tag-alias-preview, POST /promote-tag-alias preview then apply alias promotion into a canonical tag
POST /demote-tag-preview, POST /demote-tag preview then apply canonical-tag demotion, including alias and assignment rewrites
POST /mutate-tag-preview, POST /mutate-tag preview then apply canonical edit, rename/rewrite when explicitly allowed, or delete

Registry and alias import confirmation is browser-owned; those imports do not have separate HTTP preview endpoints. Direct write failure preserves the current manual-patch fallback for registry and alias create/import/edit/delete. Series Tag Editor direct write failure switches to its offline-session path.

The retained Python boundary is:

  • tag_source_paths.py: source and public Series-index paths;
  • tag_source_model.py: IDs, groups, weights, aliases, import limits, payload loading, and assignment-session validation;
  • tag_assignment_service.py: Series-first assignment save and import preview/apply planning;
  • tag_registry_mutations.py, tag_alias_mutations.py, and tag_promotion_mutations.py: registry, alias, promote/demote, and dependent reference plans;
  • tag_write_transactions.py: single-file atomic replacement and multi-file staging, replacement, and rollback;
  • tag_activity.py: write-only activity attachment;
  • tag_routes.py: the 14 POST paths;
  • tag_write_api/: HTTP request/result adapters.

Tag Policy

Retained tag policy currently lives in analytics-app/app/frontend/config/analytics-config.json:

  • ordered and coverage groups: subject, domain, form, theme;
  • completeness denominator 4, tag bonus maximum 0.25, bonus cap at 6 total tags, score cap 1.0;
  • red when total tags equal 0 or unknown tags are greater than 0;
  • amber when groups present are at most 1, total tags are below 3, or both form and theme are absent;
  • green as fallback.

Allowed canonical groups remain registry policy in tag-registry.json, with the Python model fallback matching the same four groups. The route registry, shell paths, public data paths, media settings, and Analytics host/runtime projection are not tag policy and must not move into the focused Studio tag config.

Activity And Offline Session

The activity contract currently registers 13 write actions:

  • Series Tags: import-series-tag-assignments;
  • Series Tag Editor: save-series-tags;
  • Tag Registry: import-tag-registry, create-tag, edit-tag, delete-tag, and demote-registry-tag;
  • Tag Aliases: import-tag-aliases, create-tag-alias, edit-tag-alias, delete-tag-alias, promote-tag-alias, and demote-aliases-tag.

All use script purpose save-tag-data, skip no-change activity, and attach only on non-dry-run write paths. The browser supplies page, action, route, control, correlation, and record identity. The service derives tag or alias record groups where present and writes through the unified Studio activity owner.

The Series Tag Editor reuses one initiating activity context across a save that may issue a Series request plus multiple Work requests. Preserve that behavior when the API moves.

The offline assignment contract is:

  • local-storage key dotlineform.studio.tagAssignmentsOffline.v1;
  • envelope version tag_assignments_offline_v1;
  • top-level updated_at_utc and series map;
  • each staged Series entry stores base_series_updated_at_utc, base_row_snapshot, staged_row, and staged_at_utc;
  • Series rows contain weighted tags and optional Work rows with weighted tags; tag rows preserve optional alias context.

The Series Tags route owns export, copy, download, clear, preview, explicit conflict resolution, apply, and removal of only successfully imported matching session entries.

Frontend And CSS Attribution

Retain the five route templates and the live tag behavior behind:

  • analysis-tag-scoring.js;
  • analytics-tag-editor.js plus its domain, interactions, modals, render, route-state, save, save-controller, state, and suggestions modules;
  • series-tag-editor-page.js, series-tags.js, series-tags-import-workflow.js, series-tags-modals.js, and series-tags-render.js;
  • all tag-aliases-*, tag-registry-*, tag-assignments-offline*, tag-modal-shell.js, and tag-route-save-session.js modules;
  • the tag-relevant text and role/class contracts currently in analytics-ui-text.js and analytics-ui.js.

Adapt rather than transfer Analytics infrastructure:

  • replace analytics-config.js, analytics-data.js, analytics-transport.js, analytics-route-state.js, analytics-modal.js, and analytics-activity-context.js with Studio-owned config, service, transport, ready/busy, modal, and activity integration;
  • use Studio's existing catalogue-public-links.js owner instead of copying the Analytics duplicate;
  • retire analytics-app.js, analytics-navigation.js, analytics-route-registry.js, analytics-route-templates.js, analytics-theme.js, the Analytics shell/home template, and analytics-tag-editor-index.js; the last module has no active importer.

From analytics.css, retain only rules attributable to the five tag routes: the tag editor/page, groups, filters, coverage/RAG, registry, aliases, Series Tags, tag-specific field/list, and required modal content rules. Re-express them under Studio ownership where existing Studio shell or component styles do not already cover them.

Do not transfer:

  • Analytics root, shell, header, navigation, theme-toggle, or home styling;
  • the .dataSharingReview* and .dataSharingPrepare* blocks beginning at current lines 1097 and 1325, their shared-selectable-list overrides, or their responsive continuations;
  • the unreferenced document modal-width variant;
  • the shared selectable-list shell dependency, which is now referenced only by stale Data Sharing CSS and Analytics shell asset registration.

Tests And External Consumers

Current Analytics-owned Python tests:

  • server/runtime config, route registry, static-path policy, reads, and all API adapters;
  • source model and limits;
  • assignment save and import preview/apply;
  • registry and alias import/mutation/rewrite;
  • promote/demote plans;
  • atomic single- and multi-file transactions with rollback;
  • activity attachment and route ownership.

Current Analytics smokes cover registry, alias, assignment, and promote/demote APIs; all five route boundaries; groups reads; Series Tags rendering; shared tag-route browser modules; and Tag Aliases/Series Tag Editor ready-state behavior.

Non-Analytics dependencies that must be retargeted:

  • studio/services/catalogue/generate_work_pages.py imports the Analytics path module and may create or normalize missing Series assignment rows during selected Series-page generation;
  • studio/services/catalogue/catalogue_cleanup.py imports the same path module and removes Work overrides or Series rows during catalogue deletion;
  • admin-app/checks/audit_site_consistency.py imports the path module and validates assignment schema plus Series/Work references;
  • Admin projection, route, target-map, source-classification, activity, and check configuration currently names Analytics data, assets, routes, or scope;
  • admin-app/commands/run_checks.py owns the current Analytics Python targets and analytics-smoke profile;
  • bin/local-analytics, bin/local-all, bin/local-studio, local-browser asset checks, and Admin app links still describe the Analytics runtime.

The public catalogue generator currently uses assignments only to ensure a canonical Series row exists; it does not project tag rows into public Series or Work JSON. This is the current basis for expecting unchanged public catalogue artifacts during the ownership move.

Package Boundary

No live Analytics source, route, API, frontend module, or tag service imports a tag-package or document-package subsystem. Analytics server tests retain negative assertions that Data Sharing and document-package paths are not composed.

Integrated document packages remain separately owned under docs-viewer/services/docs_document_packages/ and docs-viewer/runtime/js/packages/. They share no runtime or source authority with the tag cutover and do not move with it.

The Data Sharing selectors still present in analytics.css are retirement residue, not evidence of a package dependency.

Baseline Evidence

  • python -m pytest analytics-app/tests/python -q: 58 passed;
  • python -m pytest admin-app/tests/python/test_activity_contract.py -q: 1 passed;
  • admin-app/commands/run_checks.py --profile analytics-smoke --run-id tms-p0-freeze: 10/10 passed;
  • profile summary: var/admin/test-runs/tms-p0-freeze/summary.md.

These results establish the pre-cutover Python, API, route, browser-module, and activity baseline. They are not evidence for Studio ownership, which begins in TMS-P1.
